title: services.json
description: A repo's declaration, ahead of time, of what the node's server may do with it (PLAN-routing-tree.md §14.8): the command its `check` service runs, the CLI and verbs its `write` service may run, the tags it owns for `route`. It is also the repo's registration as a tool (PLAN-architecture.md §6 "Every tool registered", §9 step 10.1): its one-line `description`, the `stores` it owns and the `shapes` it reads and emits; the workspace list (`checks tools`) is collected from these entries, never written by hand. Setup installs the skeleton (the repo's name and its `check` entry only); the repo's owner fills it; the node's registry is the union of these files, held equal by `registry-matches`. `services-valid` validates this file against this schema with checkslib/checkjson.py (which refuses a keyword it does not enforce) and enforces each `x-rules` id in checkslib/contract.py; `registered` (roles:lag) asks for the description and for every store cli.json declares. This is tools/checks' reading of §14.8's prose; the hub's registry plan may refine it.

name.description: The repo's name, as setup wrote it.

description.description: One line saying what the tool is for: the stub of its registration (PLAN-architecture.md §6). Optional here; `registered` reports a repo without one.

stores.description: The stores this repo owns, by the same names cli.json's `store` gives them; `[]` says it owns none.

shapes.description: The data-bridge schema ids this repo reads and emits (the pipe stages of PLAN-job-sourcing.md §2), where it has any. The ids are not resolved against data-bridge here.

reads.description: Schema ids of the records it takes in.

emits.description: Schema ids of the records it puts out.

services.description: One entry per program the server may run here, with the verbs it may pass it.

service.description: `check`: the repo's own check command (the server's check service runs it). `write`: a gated CLI the write service runs for a read-only role. `route` and `hook` are the node's own services, never a repo's.

run.description: The executable, a path relative to the repo root.

verbs.description: The subcommands the server may pass `run`; each must be one `<run> help` lists.

tags.description: Message tags this repo owns for `route`.

x-rules.one-check: exactly one entry has service `check`: the command the server's check service runs
x-rules.run-inside: every `run` is a relative path inside the repo: not absolute, no `..` segment
x-rules.verb-implemented: every verb is a command `<run> help` lists (checkslib/helptext.py reads the help)
x-rules.unique: no (service, run) pair twice, no verb twice in one entry, no tag twice, no store twice, no shape id twice in `reads` or in `emits`
x-rules.write-declared: a `write` entry whose `run` is the CLI cli.json names may pass only verbs cli.json declares: nothing undeclared reaches the store
x-rules.description-one-line: `description` is one line with words on it: no line break, not blank
x-rules.stores-declared: every `stores` entry is an entry of cli.json's `store` (compared normalised, `./a` is `a`): no store is owned that cli.json does not declare
